source.title: A solution to an open problem on lower against number in graphs

accepted.question_text: Let G be a finite connected graph with vertex set V(G), and for each vertex v let N[v] be the closed neighborhood consisting of v and all vertices adjacent to v. A function f from V(G) to {-1, 1} is negative if the sum of f(u) over all u in N[v] is at most 1 for every vertex v. A negative function f is maximal if there is no distinct negative function g such that g(v) is at least f(v) for every vertex v. The lower against number beta_N^*(G) is the minimum value of the total weight sum_{v in V(G)} f(v), taken over all maximal negative functions f. What is the sharp lower bound for beta_N^*(G) for an arbitrary general graph G, expressed in terms of the order of G and the maximum degree of G?

evidence.quote: We solve the problem by establishing a tight lower bound on lower against number of a general graph in terms of order and maximum degree.
